quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road must:

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
Assume that other drivers will make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when it is clear to do so.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road without bicycle lanes and see a bicyclist ahead going the same direction. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down and wait until no traffic is coming, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bicyclist.
Drive straight. The bicyclist must get out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
Honk to warn the bicyclist you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait until no traffic is coming, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bicyclist.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicyclist the same way you pass any vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space on regular roads or 5 feet on higher-speed roads. Do not honk unnecessarily, as it may startle the rider and cause a crash.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: If you are involved in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Do not stand in traffic lanes—you could be hit by another vehicle. Turn off damaged vehicle engines.

questions.question: You notice your vehicle has a defect that could affect safe driving. You should:

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you can afford it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any defect that could affect safe driving must be fixed as soon as possible. Do not drive the vehicle until it is repaired.

questions.question: Signs of a drunk driver include:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include weaving, driving too fast or too slow, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you must:

options.text: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Slow down and look for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
questions.explanation: Any eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must stop completely and check for pedestrians and other traffic. Wait for the intersection to clear before you go.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot before changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: An "End school zone" sign means:

options.text: The speed limit is now 20 mph.
You are entering a reduced speed zone.
You are leaving a reduced speed zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are leaving a reduced speed zone.
questions.explanation: The "End school zone" sign shows where the reduced speed zone ends. Follow the school zone speed limit during the times indicated on the sign.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down on wet or slushy roads.
Watch for standing water and puddles.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, your car takes longer to stop and may skid on turns. Do not use cruise control on wet or icy roads. Reduce your speed and drive with care.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass. You may only cross these lines to make a left turn or pass pedestrians, cyclists, or scooter riders when it is safe.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or a gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not try to go around the gate.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:

options.text: Pull over to the side and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop.

questions.question: An intersection has no signs or signals. A vehicle to your right arrives at the same time as you. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection.
Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
Drive through and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk your horn and drive through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on the right has the right of way. Wait for that vehicle to pass safely before you go.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check them.

questions.question: How can you stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Do not drive next to them and do not drive too close behind them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive next to them and do not drive too close behind them.
questions.explanation: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots on the sides and rear. Avoid driving next to them and do not tailgate.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if no other cars are visible.
Signal only if other cars are visible.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if no other cars are visible.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb. Make this a habit every time.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails are ahead and to the right.
A hotel is ahead and to the right.
A hospital is ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A hospital is ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that hospital emergency services are located to the right.

questions.question: Mixing drugs with alcohol:

options.text: Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
Reduces the effects of alcohol on driving.
Does not affect your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases your risk of crashing.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter) can damage your brain function and hurt your driving ability. Mixing drugs and alcohol increases your crash risk.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to prevent accidents.
Getting ahead of bad drivers in traffic.
Driving very close to the vehicle in front of you.
Quickly changing lanes to avoid traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you see dangerous situations early and act to prevent accidents. It helps you deal with aggressive, careless, or unsafe drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill and see a heavy truck ahead of you. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles often go slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. Be careful when approaching them from behind. On a hill with poor visibility, it is illegal to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: A driver taking a non-prescription drug should:

options.text: Read the labels on the drug before driving.
Continue to drive no matter what the label says.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the labels on the drug before driving.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter drugs for colds or allergies can affect your driving. Always read the label for warnings. If you are not sure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if it is safe to drive while taking the medication.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol and drugs can:
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the effects of both.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs increases the effects of both. It is unsafe to drive after using either one alone. It is even more dangerous to use them together.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Are better drivers because they are not hungry.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have trouble controlling their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers doing these things have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show they are wrong.
Do something to get back at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and get out of the aggressive driver's way. Trying to get even with them makes the situation worse and more dangerous.

questions.question: Two solid white lines mark the boundaries of a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know that:

options.text: Motor vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show where pedestrians should cross safely. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.question: You see the driver ahead using one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:

options.text: Know they are not paying full attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving by talking to passengers, looking for things, or daydreaming. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space because they are more likely to cause an accident.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: U-turns are not allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash through it means the action is prohibited. You cannot make a U-turn where this sign is posted.

questions.question: You may turn right on red:

options.text: After a complete stop and only if it is safe for pedestrians and other vehicles.
Where a sign says no right turn on red.
Without coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: After a complete stop and only if it is safe for pedestrians and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: You can turn right on red after a full stop, but only if there is no sign prohibiting it and it is safe. Watch for pedestrians crossing in front of you.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely:
questions.correctAnswerText: Blind.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians who are blind and using a white cane or guide dog.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:

options.text: Slow down gradually and check the rearview mirror.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal 3 to 5 seconds before turning. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. On multi-lane roads, move to the left lane before the intersection. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then turn when it is safe.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Stop only if other cars are approaching.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a bicycle crossing or path. Drive carefully in this area because bicycles often cross or ride near traffic here.

questions.question: Defensive driving is:

options.text: Using safe strategies to prevent crashes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using safe strategies to prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means using safe strategies to prevent crashes. Adjust your driving based on weather, how you feel, and what other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians are doing.

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout:

options.text: Remove your foot from the gas pedal.
Slow down gradually and pull to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Remove your foot from the gas pedal. Do not brake right away. Slow down gradually, then gently apply the brakes and pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of their way.
questions.explanation: Get out of an aggressive driver's way. Avoid eye contact. Speeding up may anger them more and increase danger.

questions.question: When driving on highways:

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stay alert and ready to react on highways. Avoid looking at one thing for more than a few seconds to prevent highway hypnosis.

questions.question: When using a roundabout, drivers should:

options.text: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection with no traffic signal. Enter from the right, yield to traffic already inside, and follow the circle counterclockwise until you reach your road.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Fog reduces visibility of vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. Drive slowly and carefully. Do not use high beams. Low beams work better in fog.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Pull next to them and yell.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let it go.
questions.explanation: Do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Let it go and keep driving safely to avoid road rage.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, pulling away from a curb, or merging into traffic is:

options.text: Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots before changing lanes. Look over your shoulder toward the next lane. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: When you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If another driver is threatening you or driving dangerously, stay calm. Slow down and let them pass. Create distance between your vehicle and theirs. Do not make eye contact or make gestures.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the driver who drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: A serious traffic safety problem.
questions.explanation: Driving while drunk is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking alcohol or taking drugs. Impaired driving is dangerous to you and everyone on the road.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Roundabout ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a roundabout is ahead. Enter a roundabout slowly and yield to traffic already in it.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.
The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and other drugs together can increase how much they impair you. For example, one drink plus a cold medicine could affect you as much as several drinks alone.

questions.question: You may drive across a dashed white line:

options.text: When it is safe to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Broken white lines separate traffic lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross dashed lines to pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
Copy what surrounding traffic is doing, despite the flagger's instructions.
Assume the flagger is not supposed to be directing traffic.
Follow the laws that would be in place if the area was not under construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
questions.explanation: Follow instructions from signs, flaggers, or police in construction zones. Slow down when directed. Failing to follow their directions is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: Passing is prohibited:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass another vehicle on hills, curves, at intersections, or at railroad crossings. Passing in these places is illegal and unsafe.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams turned on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams turned on.
questions.explanation: When stopped on the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and low beam headlights. Make sure other drivers can see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers what they must and must not do. This sign means left turns are not allowed.
